statement.p: Consider a rectangular coordinate system with origin at the center of the earth, z-axis through the North Pole, and x-axis through the prime-meridian. Find the rectangular coordinates of London, England (51^{\circ}32' \text{N}, 0^{\circ}5' \text{W}). A minute is 1/60^{\circ}. Assume the earth is a sphere of radius R=6367 \text{ km}.
Usage: To enter a point, for example (x,y,z), type "(x, y, z)".

static.solution:
(\theta,\phi) for London. Since it's longitude lies to the west of Greenwich, that is, in the negative \theta direction, \theta=360^{\circ}-0.0833333^{\circ}=359.917^{\circ}. The latitude is north of the equator, hence \phi=90^{\circ}-51.5333^{\circ}=38.4667^{\circ}.
We now use the formulas of x, y, and z in terms of \rho, \theta, and \phi to find the rectangular coordinates: \begin{array}{rcl} x \amp =\amp \rho\sin\phi\cos\theta=6367\sin38.4667^{\circ}\cos359.917^{\circ}= 3960.65 \\ y \amp =\amp \rho\sin\phi\sin\theta=6367\sin38.4667^{\circ}\sin359.917^{\circ}= -5.72436 \\ z \amp =\amp \rho\cos\phi = 6367\cos38.4667^{\circ}= 4985.17 \end{array}
